f.title: Process health data for public health purposes only where necessary and under a health professional or a person owing confidentiality
f.statement: The public health condition for processing special category data (such as health data in pharmacovigilance) is met only if the processing is necessary for reasons of public interest in the area of public health and is carried out by or under the responsibility of a health professional, or by another person who in the circumstances owes a duty of confidentiality under an enactment or rule of law.
f.topic: Privacy: public health condition for health data
f.legal_basis: DPA 2018 s.10(2), Sch. 1 para. 3; UK GDPR Art. 9(2)(i)
f.applicability: Processing of health data for reasons of public interest in the area of public health (UK GDPR Art. 9(2)(i)), e.g. pharmacovigilance and the safety of medicinal products
f.exceptions: The processing must be carried out by or under the responsibility of a health professional, or by a person owing a statutory or common-law duty of confidentiality.
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Case processing & follow-up

f.title: Process special category data for research only where necessary, in line with UK GDPR Article 84B and in the public interest
f.statement: The research condition for processing special category data is met only if the processing is necessary for archiving purposes, scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes, is carried out in accordance with Article 84B of the UK GDPR, and is in the public interest.
f.topic: Privacy: research condition for health data
f.legal_basis: DPA 2018 s.10(2), Sch. 1 para. 4; UK GDPR Art. 9(2)(j), Art. 84B
f.applicability: Processing of health data in clinical trials, post-authorisation safety studies and other scientific research (UK GDPR Art. 9(2)(j))
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Epidemiology / safety studies; Clinical safety monitoring

f.title: Have an appropriate policy document in place when relying on a substantial public interest condition
f.statement: Except as otherwise provided, a substantial public interest condition in Part 2 of Schedule 1 is met only if, when the processing is carried out, the controller has an appropriate policy document in place (see paragraph 39).
f.clause: Schedule 1 Part 2, paragraph 5 Requirement for an appropriate policy document
f.applicability: Processing of special category data in reliance on a substantial public interest condition in Schedule 1 Part 2 (UK GDPR Art. 9(2)(g))
f.exceptions: Except as otherwise provided in Part 2 (e.g. paragraph 10(2) disclosures to a competent authority).

rows.quote: (1) Except as otherwise provided, a condition in this Part of this Schedule is met only if, when the processing is carried out, the controller has an appropriate policy document in place (see paragraph 39 in Part 4 of this Schedule).

f.title: Rely on the statutory purposes condition only where processing is necessary for a statutory function and for substantial public interest
f.statement: The statutory and government purposes condition is met if the processing is necessary for the exercise of a function conferred on a person by an enactment or rule of law (or a function of the Crown, a Minister or a government department) and is necessary for reasons of substantial public interest. As a Part 2 condition it also requires an appropriate policy document (paragraph 5).
f.clause: Schedule 1 Part 2, paragraph 6 Statutory etc and government purposes
f.legal_basis: DPA 2018 Sch. 1 para. 6; UK GDPR Art. 9(2)(g)
f.applicability: Processing of special category data necessary for a function conferred by an enactment or rule of law (UK GDPR Art. 9(2)(g)), e.g. statutory pharmacovigilance functions

f.title: Write an appropriate policy document covering Article 5 compliance procedures and retention and erasure policies
f.statement: Where a Schedule 1 condition requires an appropriate policy document, the controller must have produced a document that explains its procedures for securing compliance with the Article 5 UK GDPR principles for processing under that condition, and its policies on retention and erasure of the personal data processed under the condition, giving an indication of how long such data is likely to be retained.
f.clause: Schedule 1 Part 4, paragraph 39 Requirement to have an appropriate policy document in place
f.applicability: Processing in reliance on a Schedule 1 condition that requires an appropriate policy document (para. 1, Part 2 conditions)

rows.quote:
(39) The controller has an appropriate policy document in place in relation to the processing of personal data in reliance on a condition described in paragraph 38 if the controller has produced a document which—
(a) explains the controller's procedures for securing compliance with the principles in Article 5 of the UK GDPR (principles relating to processing of personal data) in connection with the processing of personal data in reliance on the condition in question, and (b) explains the controller's policies as regards the retention and erasure of personal data processed in reliance on the condition, giving an indication of how long such personal data is likely to be retained.
rows.location: Schedule 1 Part 4, paragraph 39 Requirement to have an appropriate policy document in place
rows.review_note: Review: paragraph 39 defines when a document counts; stated as the duty it sets the scope of (audit rule on definitions). Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Retain, review and provide the appropriate policy document to the Commissioner on request until 6 months after the processing ends
f.statement: Where personal data is processed in reliance on a condition requiring an appropriate policy document, the controller must, during the relevant period, retain the document, review and (if appropriate) update it from time to time, and make it available to the Information Commission on request without charge. The relevant period begins when the controller starts processing in reliance on the condition and ends 6 months after the controller ceases such processing.
f.clause: Schedule 1 Part 4, paragraph 40 Additional safeguard: retention of appropriate policy document
f.applicability: Processing in reliance on a Schedule 1 condition that requires an appropriate policy document

rows.deadline: Retain from the start of the processing until the end of 6 months after the controller ceases the processing
rows.quote:
(1) Where personal data is processed in reliance on a condition described in paragraph 38, the controller must during the relevant period—
(a) retain the appropriate policy document, (b) review and (if appropriate) update it from time to time, and (c) make it available to the Commission, on request, without charge. (2) “Relevant period”, in relation to the processing of personal data in reliance on a condition described in paragraph 38, means a period which—
(a) begins when the controller starts to carry out processing of personal data in reliance on that condition, and (b) ends at the end of the period of 6 months beginning when the controller ceases to carry out such processing.
rows.location: Schedule 1 Part 4, paragraph 40 Additional safeguard: retention of appropriate policy document
rows.review_note: Review: "the Commission" in the consolidated text is the Information Commission. Double-check: the 6-month rule is a retention period after cessation, structured as months from cessation.

deadline_rule.clock_start: beginning when the controller ceases to carry out such processing
deadline_rule.applies_to: Retention of the appropriate policy document after the processing ceases

f.title: Record in the Article 30 record the Schedule 1 condition relied on, the Article 6 basis and adherence to retention policies
f.statement: Where the controller (or its representative) keeps an Article 30 UK GDPR record of processing carried out in reliance on a condition requiring an appropriate policy document, the record must include which condition is relied on, how the processing satisfies Article 6 (lawfulness of processing), and whether the personal data is retained and erased in line with the policy document and, if not, the reasons for not following those policies.
f.clause: Schedule 1 Part 4, paragraph 41 Additional safeguard: record of processing
f.legal_basis: DPA 2018 Sch. 1 para. 41; UK GDPR Art. 30
f.applicability: Article 30 records for processing in reliance on a Schedule 1 condition that requires an appropriate policy document

rows.quote:
(41) A record maintained by the controller, or the controller's representative, under Article 30 of the UK GDPR in respect of the processing of personal data in reliance on a condition described in paragraph 38 must include the following information—
(a) which condition is relied on, (b) how the processing satisfies Article 6 of the UK GDPR (lawfulness of processing), and (c) whether the personal data is retained and erased in accordance with the policies described in paragraph 39(b) and, if it is not, the reasons for not following those policies.
rows.location: Schedule 1 Part 4, paragraph 41 Additional safeguard: record of processing
